scenario: EGFR kinase hit-finding bench (PDB 1M17) for chain vina_virtual_screening_bench

sources.verified: TITLE EGFR tyrosine kinase domain with 4-anilinoquinazoline inhibitor erlotinib; chain A; HET AQ4 A 999 (29 heavy atoms = erlotinib)

sources.derived_from: 1M17.pdb HETATM AQ4 A 999 (29 heavy atoms, no H), redocking reference

sources.rule: query == 'Epidermal growth factor receptor', affinity_type == IC50, plain numeric value <= 100 nM (qualified '<'/'>' dropped), median per BindingDB monomer id, one per InChIKey connectivity block, MW 250-500 and <=38 heavy atoms (approved drugs exempt), 55 picked by MaxMin Morgan2 diversity over a seeded 600-molecule subset after force-including the approved drugs

sources.dataset: ZINC250k: 250k drug-like ZINC-derived molecules (Gomez-Bombarelli et al., ACS Cent Sci 2018); first 90,000 of a seeded shuffle used as candidate pool
sources.licence: ZINC is free for use (zinc.docking.org terms); the hosting repository is MIT licensed. Redistribution of ~250 SMILES subset assumed acceptable; confirm before external release.

deviations_from_plan: ChEMBL REST (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/api/data) returned HTTP 500 on every endpoint incl. /status, with the generic service-unavailable page, for >30 min on 2026-11-01; actives therefore come from BindingDB (which itself curates ChEMBL/literature IC50) instead of ChEMBL. Ids are BindingDB monomer ids (BDBM...), not CHEMBL ids.

DUD-E (https://dude.docking.org/targets/egfr/decoys_final.ism) timed out (30 s, both http and https); ZINC15 substance search is behind a captcha. Fallback decoys documented below. DUD-E licence not checked because it was unreachable.

decoy_matching_rule.per_active: up to 5 decoys (cap keeps library ~300 for dev docking)
decoy_matching_rule.properties_rdkit: MolWt, Crippen logP, Lipinski HBD, Lipinski HBA, rotatable bonds (CalcNumRotatableBonds) of the largest fragment
decoy_matching_rule.topological_dissimilarity: max Morgan(r=2,2048) Tanimoto to ANY of the 3396 candidate EGFR actives must be < 0.35
decoy_matching_rule.uniqueness: no decoy shares an InChIKey or canonical SMILES with any BindingDB EGFR active (checked against all 3396 candidates, not just the 55 picked)
decoy_matching_rule.limits: some actives (e.g. erlotinib, osimertinib) got 0 matched decoys because the dissimilarity filter removes quinazoline-like candidates; decoys are pooled, so the library still holds 246 decoys (<5 per active on average is not reached for all). Decoys are NOT experimentally confirmed non-binders (property-matched, topologically dissimilar only), as in DUD-E.

reference_split.rule: 5 random (seeded) non-approved actives; marked label=reference in labels.csv; excluded from library.smi and from scoring
